questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
This was first and foremost an opportunity to learn. Boston  is the global capital for economics, which was what motivated by application. Courses, faculty, and seminars on the university and other universities, and open access to these universities, were primary contributors. 
Specifically, I enjoyed the seminars at BU, HU and MIT in theoretical and empirical microeconomics.
Culture, infrastructure and such were considered somewhat, but merely required a passable level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very expensive for generally poor levels of food, transport and living accomodations. Furthermore, forced healthcare insurance with no functionality added unneccessary expense at no gain. BU and KU did very little to facilitate social connections or preparing us for the trip and providing guidance in terms of choosing courses, and navigating various practical aspects of the trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Generally difficult, and I had to find out about information when I arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None that I could use.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Social events and provision of information would be very much appreciated.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, but stupidly expensive and of poor quality.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don´t expect much.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process itself was easy, but there is essentially 0 informaiton available online, and actually 0 information on the course registration website, which makes it a tedious process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You are presented with a big database of all the courses at the university, and then have to scroll through pages in alphabetical order to get the one you want, and when you have clicked all the courses, you have to click confirm, and the page is reset.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't bother with code 101-499 courses, they are generally just a tool to get ECTS without any work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took code 700 courses, which are intended for PhD students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Neither, Ba and MA classes were too easy, so had to resort to PhD courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar, although I had world class professors teaching my courses, which could be felt.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Health insurance and other university fees

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than expected, especially rent and health insurance, although 50 meal dining plan proved a good way to save money, as you can eat for 2 days in one sitting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was okay, but access was limited by poor infrastructure in the city and inconvenient facilities and time tables.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Difficult, people are generally very superficial and loud. Local customs were also difficult to adjust to, as I often felt harassed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join student bodies and clubs, and use student discounts, although it is difficult to get to know the locals, as they are not particularly welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do not bother with code 101-499 courses.
2) Go to BSO and similar using student discounts
3) You can freely join lectures and seminars at Harvard University and MIT as you please, if you ask nicely

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use 50 meal dining plan and pack food into your backpack with plastic sipper bags so get inexpensive meals. Off-campus housing is bad, but on-campus housing is likely worse.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seminars at BU, HU and MIT

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The food, eating it and passing it through.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
